learn.title: How Solar PV Panels Generate Electricity
learn.intro: Solar energy is a cornerstone of the global energy transition, providing a way to harvest abundant sunlight into usable power. Understanding the physics behind solar panels is essential to appreciating how we can decarbonize our electricity grids and reduce reliance on fossil fuels through scalable, renewable technology.
learn.c1_text: Think of sunlight as a stream of tiny energy packets called photons. When these photons hit a solar cell, they knock electrons loose from their atoms, much like a cue ball hitting other billiard balls on a table, initiating the flow of electricity.
learn.c2_text: Solar cells use semiconductor materials, typically silicon, to create an internal electric field. This field acts like a one-way street, forcing the loose electrons to move in a specific direction, creating a direct current (DC) that we can use.
learn.c3_text: Most homes use alternating current (AC), so the DC power from panels must pass through an inverter. This device converts the energy so it can power your appliances or feed back into the local electrical grid.
learn.stat1: Solar PV capacity is growing exponentially worldwide
learn.stat2: Photons carry discrete packets of energy
learn.stat3: Silicon is the most common semiconductor used
learn.stat4: Inverters convert DC to AC power

learn.title: Rooftop Solar and Net Metering in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar is transforming consumers into 'prosumers' in India. By installing panels on homes and businesses, we reduce the burden on central grids and utilize existing urban surfaces, making the energy transition decentralized and much more resilient for millions of people.
learn.c1_text: Rooftop solar involves installing PV modules on existing structures. It is like having a mini power plant on your roof that works silently, reducing your dependence on external electricity providers and lowering your monthly utility bills significantly.
learn.c2_text: Net metering is a billing mechanism that credits solar owners for the excess electricity they export to the grid. It turns your meter into a two-way street, tracking both what you consume and what you contribute.
learn.c3_text: The MNRE promotes rooftop solar through various schemes to achieve India's ambitious renewable targets. Net metering policies vary by state, helping India tap into vast urban rooftop potential to meet growing national energy demands.
learn.stat1: India: Massive push for rooftop solar adoption
learn.stat2: Prosumers: Consumers who also produce energy

learn.title: Green Ammonia: The Clean Fuel Future
learn.intro: Decarbonizing heavy industries like shipping and large-scale agriculture is incredibly difficult with electricity alone. Green ammonia offers a high-density energy carrier that can replace fossil fuels, playing a vital role in a net-zero global economy.
learn.c1_text: Green ammonia starts with electrolysis, using renewable electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen. Think of it as using clean energy to 'unzip' water molecules to capture the hydrogen needed for the next step.
learn.c2_text: The captured hydrogen is combined with nitrogen from the air using the Haber-Bosch process. When powered by renewables, this produces ammonia (NH3) without the massive CO2 emissions typically associated with traditional chemical manufacturing.
learn.c3_text: Ammonia is a perfect candidate for zero-carbon shipping fuel because it is easier to store than liquid hydrogen. It also serves as a carbon-free feedstock for sustainable fertilizers, crucial for global food security.
learn.stat1: Ammonia is a high-density energy carrier

learn.title: Second Life EV Batteries for Grid Storage
learn.intro: As electric vehicle adoption surges, we face a question: what happens to batteries when they are no longer fit for cars? 'Second life' applications provide a sustainable solution, turning waste into a resource for the grid.
learn.c1_text: When an EV battery drops to about 70-80% of its original capacity, it is no longer ideal for driving. It's like a marathon runner who can no longer sprint but can still walk long distances easily.
learn.c2_text: These 'etired' batteries can be repurposed for stationary grid storage. They act like giant reservoirs, soaking up excess solar or wind energy during the day and releasing it when demand peaks at night.
learn.c3_text: Reusing batteries extends their lifecycle and reduces the environmental impact of mining new materials. This circular approach lowers the total lifecycle cost of energy storage systems globally.
learn.stat2: Reduces need for new raw materials

learn.title: How Electric Vehicles Work
learn.intro: Electric vehicles (EVs) represent a fundamental shift in how we move. By replacing internal combustion engines with electric motors, we can drastically reduce tailpipe emissions and improve urban air quality, accelerating the transition to sustainable transport.
learn.c1_text: An EV motor uses electricity from the battery to create magnetic fields. These fields interact to create motion, much like how two magnets can push each other away, turning the wheels of the car.
learn.c2_text: When you lift your foot off the accelerator, the motor runs in reverse, acting as a generator. This converts the car's kinetic energy back into electricity, recharging the battery and slowing the vehicle down.
learn.c3_text: EVs can be charged via various levels of power, from slow home AC chargers to fast DC chargers. This versatility allows for both overnight charging and quick top-ups during long journeys.
learn.stat3: AC and DC charging options available

learn.title: HVDC: Long-Distance Power Transmission
learn.intro: To integrate massive amounts of wind and solar power from remote areas to cities, we need advanced transmission. High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) is the key technology that makes long-distance, efficient energy transport possible.
learn.c1_text: While most local grids use Alternating Current (AC), HVDC uses Direct Current. Think of AC as a wave moving back and forth, while DC is a steady, direct stream of water flowing in one direction.
learn.c3_text: HVDC allows us to connect remote offshore wind farms or desert solar plants to distant urban centers. This connectivity is vital for creating a stable, interconnected global energy grid.
